Based on the graph, directly write the range of values of $x$ for which $k_1x+b>\frac{k_2}{x}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Observing the graph, the range of $x$ for $k_1x+b>\frac{k_2}{x}$ is \boxed{-2<x<0} or \boxed{x>1}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is an obliquely upward straight line y=k_1x+b, and two branch curves of an inverse proportional function y=k_2/x. The right branch of the inverse proportional curve is in the first quadrant, the left branch is in the third quadrant, and the y-axis x=0 is the vertical asymptote of the inverse proportional function. The straight line intersects the right branch at point A, and intersects the left branch at point B; the problem gives that the x-coordinate of A is 1, and the x-coordinate of B is -2. Then reason: comparing k_1x+b and k_2/x is to see whether the straight line is above the inverse proportional curve at the same x. Since the intersection points and the asymptote divide the x-axis into four intervals (-∞,-2), (-2,0), (0,1), (1,+∞). From the image it can be seen that on (-∞,-2) the straight line is below the left branch curve; on (-2,0) the straight line is above the left branch curve; on (0,1) the straight line is below the right branch curve; on (1,+∞) the straight line is above the right branch curve. Therefore the range of x satisfying k_1x+b>k_2/x is -2<x<0 or x>1.
